meta.title: Lattis, the free and smooth spreadsheet with the power of a database
meta.desc: Lattis is a free desktop spreadsheet, smoother than the competition, that adds everything a database can do: SQL, instant pivot tables, connections to your databases, teamwork and Lua scripts.
hero.badge: Public beta available · Free for everyone
hero.title1: A spreadsheet smoother than the competition.
hero.title2: With the power<br class="hbr">of a database.
hero.sub: You keep your bearings, but everything is simpler and faster. Behind every table, a real SQL database so you get the full power of databases. And it's free!

strip.2: Your data, local or on your own server
how.title: A spreadsheet that understands your data
how.sub: No schema to draw, no wizard to follow. Lattis watches what you type and does the database work for you.
how.s1d: Enter your data anywhere on the canvas, like in any spreadsheet. Nothing gets in the way of your typing.
how.s2d: It spots the block of data, highlights the header, infers each column's type and creates the matching SQLite table.
how.s3d: Your tables are real tables: SQL, formulas, pivot tables and charts run directly on the engine.
video.title: See Lattis in action
video.sub: Short videos covering the essentials. They are coming with the first public releases.
feat.title: Everything other spreadsheets don't do
feat.sub: Every table is a real SQLite table. You keep the grid, and you gain everything a database makes possible.
feat.1d: Several independent tables per sheet, each framed by a thin border. If one starts in A1, the sheet tab takes its name.
feat.2d: Text, integer, decimal, date, boolean. The type is detected as you type, never blocks your input, and can always be changed.
feat.3d: Everything fits in a single .lattis file, easy to send or archive, with crash recovery built in.
feat.4d: A familiar formula language with structured references such as Customers[City]. VLOOKUP becomes REFERENCE.
feat.5d: Query and edit your tables in SQL, with every object in the workbook listed right beside you.
feat.6d: Automate with db.query() and events. A safeguard stops infinite loops, so the interface never freezes.
feat.7d: Instant aggregations, displayed as a tree. Add calculated columns with a formula, such as the year of a date, to group or filter.
feat.8d: Charts fed by your data, and Document tabs to lay out your analyses.
feat.9t: AI assistant, if you want it
feat.9d: An Assistant tab that is off by default, which you can connect to your own key or account.
show.1a: The Lattis SQL tab showing a result as a grid
show.1t: SQL and grid, side by side
show.1d: Run a GROUP BY in the SQL tab and the result appears as a grid you can sort, filter and reuse.
show.2a: Pivot table and chart in Lattis
show.2d: Pivot tables and charts rely on SQLite's native aggregation. They update as soon as your data changes.
show.3d: A simple, safe API to work on your tables in the background, with a built-in reference and warnings as you type.
conn.title: Connected to your databases and your team
conn.sub: Import and refresh external data in a few clicks. Passwords stay in your computer's keychain.
conn.1d: PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite.
conn.2d: JSON REST APIs, Parquet and JSON files.
conn.3d: Lattis Server, self-hosted on PostgreSQL: live multi-user editing, roles and permissions, offline work, a Data Lake and editing from the browser. A workbook can also be shared on a network folder or a NAS.
price.title: Free. For everyone.
price.sub: No Pro edition, no subscription, no row limit. Lattis is free for individuals and companies alike, and it will stay that way.
price.i4: Your data, local or on your own server
fund.title: So who funds Lattis?
fund.sub: The software is free for everyone because those who get the most value from it contribute in other ways.
fund.1d: Companies that rely on Lattis every day can support its development with a donation.
fund.2d: Partners fund specific features or back the roadmap, in full transparency.
fund.3d: Courses to get started with Lattis, SQL or Lua automation, for teams or individuals.
fund.4d: Help with rollout, migrating your existing workbooks, connecting your databases and custom scripts.
fund.cta: Support Lattis or get in touch
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Yes. Every feature is free, for personal and professional use, with no subscription and no Pro edition. The project is funded by company donations, partnerships, training and business support.
faq.a2: On your computer. A workbook is a .lattis file containing a SQLite database. Nothing goes to a server unless you connect an external database or your own Lattis Server yourself.
faq.q3: Will my spreadsheet habits still work?
faq.a3: Yes: ribbon, context menus, shortcuts, undo and redo, familiar formulas. VLOOKUP is even converted to REFERENCE automatically.
faq.q4: Which systems does Lattis run on?
faq.a4: Windows, macOS and Linux. It is a native application built in Go with Wails and SvelteKit, without the weight of Electron.
faq.a5: Right now: a first beta is available for Windows, macOS and Linux. The Download button automatically fetches the latest version for your system.
faq.a6: Gladly: through a donation, a partnership, training for your teams or tailored support. Write to us at contact@lattis.be.

ergo.title: Simpler and smoother than the competition
ergo.sub: The same gestures, fewer steps. Lattis takes care of what other spreadsheets leave you to do by hand.
ergo.1x: Format as Table, check the range, rename it
ergo.1l: Type your data: the table is detected, framed and named for you
ergo.2l: =REFERENCE(Customers, City, A2), readable, no column number
ergo.3x: Fill it down and check it follows new rows
ergo.3l: A calculated column applies to every row automatically
ergo.4x: A date or a code can change format without warning
ergo.4l: Every column has a type, detected as you type and easy to change
ergo.5x: Pivot tables you refresh by hand
ergo.5l: SQL and instant pivot tables, up to date as soon as data changes
ergo.6x: Macros that can freeze the workbook
ergo.6l: Lua scripts with a built-in reference and a safeguard against infinite loops
arch.title: Under the hood
arch.sub: For the curious: a native application, a real database inside every file, and a self-hosted server when you work as a team.
arch.d1: Written in Go with a SvelteKit interface, brought together by Wails. A real application for Windows, macOS and Linux, light and fast, without Electron.
arch.d2: Every .lattis file holds its own SQLite database. Nothing else to install, and your data stays with the file.
arch.d3: Calculations run on the SQL engine. Lua scripts run without ever freezing the interface.
arch.d4: A built-in MCP server lets an assistant such as Claude work on the open workbook, if you turn it on.
arch.d5: For teamwork, a server you host yourself. PostgreSQL 18 is required; Docker or Kubernetes are supported. Editing from the browser too.
arch.d6: Work carries on without a network and syncs when the connection returns. Without a server, a plain shared folder or NAS is enough to work together.
ergo.7x: Identical copied sheets, updated one by one
ergo.7l: Similar sheets are grouped into one, with a “2026 ▾” selector; the tables follow it
try.line: Rather not install anything? A demo runs in your browser, no account needed.
